01 • MOTIVATION

Separate transit from local work

A carrier moves between stations; smaller arms represent local handling.

  • Global task: reach the raw, staging, machine, output and finished stations.
  • Local task: represent approach, grasp, release and handling near each station.
  • Research question: how should the two levels coordinate?
Shannu (40 seconds). Explain the carrier-assisted concept before discussing code. We investigate the architecture; we have not measured an efficiency advantage over a controlled conventional baseline.

04 • COORDINATION

Reposition only when the proxy requires it

Check target → choose motion → observe final TF → recheck

  • Locally reachable: use local visual manipulation.
  • Outside the local region: reposition the carrier, then check again.
  • Unreachable or cancelled: record a specific failure rather than pretend success.
Ayush or Shannu (45 seconds). Explain the actual decision contract. Local workspace checks are geometric proxies. The recorded scenario has five visual repositions per trial; do not call this globally optimal planning.

07 • ENGINEERING STUDIES

Explore the design space

Carrier kinematics, placement and historical mass experiments

  • 20,006 carrier configurations sampled; five assumed placements compared.
  • Three archived +10% link-mass experiments analyzed as trajectory statistics.
  • Later IK/clearance diagnostics identified limits for future designs.
Shannu (55 seconds). Show the workspace image as a kinematic study, not a guaranteed collision-free reachable volume. Mass-study recordings were not time-aligned and derived accelerations are not force/torque measurements. These studies show engineering investigation and transparent limits.
